questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. When this extra water vapour condenses into precipitation, it results in heavier rain - or, if it's cold enough, heavier snow. B. The atmosphere can store an additional 4% of water vapour for every additional 1°F of warming. C. More water evaporates from soils, plants, lakes and seas as the atmosphere warms. D. One of the most obvious indications of climate change is heavier rainfall.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. When this extra water vapour condenses into precipitation, it results in heavier rain - or, if it's cold enough, heavier snow.

B. The atmosphere can store an additional 4% of water vapour for every additional 1°F of warming.

C. More water evaporates from soils, plants, lakes and seas as the atmosphere warms.

D. One of the most obvious indications of climate change is heavier rainfall.
questions.solution:
Sentence D comes first as it introduces the topic of the paragraph, i.e., 'heavier rainfall'.

Sentences C and B form the pair CB as sentence C mentions that more water evaporates as the atmosphere warms and sentence B mentions the rate of addition of water vapour to the atmosphere.

Sentence A comes last as it informs about the impact of the extra water vapours when they condense [i.e., heavier rainfall]. This means CBD in this order explains how excess water vapours result in heavier rainfall.

So, the correct order is: DCBA.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

She said, "I am in no mood to work now."

options.text: She said that she has been in no mood to work then.
options.html: She said that she has been in no mood to work then.

options.text: She said that she was in no mood to work now.
options.html: She said that she was in no mood to work now.

options.text: She said that she was in no mood to work then.
options.html: She said that she was in no mood to work then.

options.text: She said that she has been in no mood to work now.
options.html: She said that she has been in no mood to work now.

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

Simple Present (Subject + V1 + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject +V2 + Object).

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'I am' will change to 'she was'.

'Now' will change to 'then'.

Therefore, the correct answer is (c): She said that she was in no mood to work then.

questions.question: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Manu will tell her later.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Manu will tell her later.

options.text: She will be tell later by Manu.
options.html: She will be tell later by Manu.

options.text: She will tell later by Manu.
options.html: She will tell later by Manu.

options.text: She will be told later by Manu.
options.html: She will be told later by Manu.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the Future Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is (c): She will be told later by Manu.

questions.question: Select the correct active form of the given sentence. Has the villa been occupied by them?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

Has the villa been occupied by them?
questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

In Active voice (look at the options), it should be an interrogative sentence. The answer to this question will be either "yes" or "no".

These types of sentences usually begin with a helping verb like: have, has, had.

In Passive voice, the format is: Have/Has/Had + Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + been + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case)?

Thus, the format such a sentence in Active voice is: Have/Has/Had + Subject + V3 + Object?

For example:

Has the letter been written by Rohit? (Passive)

Has Rohit written the letter? (Active)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Here, 'has' will be converted to 'have' since the sentence in the passive voice is in its present perfect form. So, past perfect ('had they occupied') will be incorrect here.

Thus, the correct answer is (c): Have they occupied the villa?

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'. After finishing high school, I plan to pursuing law.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

After finishing high school, I plan to pursuing law.
questions.solution:
The infinitive marker 'to' should be followed by the base form of verb, hence, 'pursuing' should be followed by 'pursue'.

The verb 'plan' will be followed by the infinitive 'to' only.

The correct sentence is: After finishing high school, I plan to pursue law.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Note: Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

· To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

· My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

· To vote in elections is our right. [the infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

· Radha went to the lake to fetch water. [the infinitive 'to fetch', like a noun, is the object of the verb 'went', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (water)]

· The above sentences illustrate various ways in which infinitives are used. It can both act as a noun and a verb.

Infinitive marker: A word or affix attached to the stem of a verb in order to form the full infinitive. In English, to is the infinitive marker.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. During an earthquake, / it is advised to take / cover above a table / to save your life.

questions.solution:

'Above a table' should be changed to 'under a table' to rectify the error.

The correct sentence is: During an earthquake, it is advised to take cover under a table to save your life.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He was looking into his book for the last two hours but couldn't find it.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He was looking into his book for the last two hours but couldn't find it.
questions.solution:
Look into - investigate something.

Look down on someone - to feel that someone is less important than you or does not deserve respect.

Look after - to care for or be in charge of someone or something.

Look for - attempt to find someone or something.

The latter part of the sentence mentions that the subject 'he' could not find 'it' (the book). This means the phrasal verb 'looking for' would fit here contextually.

'Looking into his book' does not fit contextually.

The correct sentence is: He was looking for his book for the last two hours but couldn't find it.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Note: Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.
